$comment: Neutral shipped <threads.h> (C11 threads) — FC17.9(a). COMPLETE on elf/pe64 (Cycle 1 non-trampoline slice + Cycle 2 D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TRAMPOLINES: thrd_create/call_once/thrd_join) and COMPLETE on macho (D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-MACHO closed — 18 non-trampoline pthread recipes + the 3 macho trampolines: thrd_create→pthread_create DIRECT-PASS, call_once→pthread_once DIRECT, thrd_join→pthread_join with a stack void* out-slot + truncate; runtime-green on a Mac). `__STDC_NO_THREADS__` is now REMOVED entirely — <threads.h> is complete on ALL legs (elf/pe64/macho), so no target defines the macro (C11 6.10.8.3). THREE-PART design (elf FFI · pe win32-synth · macho pthread-synth): on elf the C11 thread API is a DIRECT libc FFI (glibc>=2.34 exports thrd_*/mtx_*/cnd_*/tss_* from libc.so.6 — verified: readelf shows `mtx_init@@GLIBC_2.34`, a real gcc link of mtx_init WITHOUT -lpthread succeeds; the same libc.so.6 pthread.json already binds). On pe64 the CRT exports NO thrd_*, so each function is a COMPILER-SYNTHESIZED win32 shim over kernel32 (CRITICAL_SECTION / CONDITION_VARIABLE / Fls* / thread APIs — all in windows.json). On macho, libSystem exports NO C11 thrd_*/mtx_*/cnd_*/tss_* (verified — `_thrd_create` undefined at link, no <threads.h> in the SDK) but pthread IS present, so each of the 18 non-trampoline functions is a COMPILER-SYNTHESIZED pthread shim over pthread_mutex_*/pthread_cond_*/pthread_key_*/pthread_self/sched_yield (the Darwin analog of pe's kernel32 shim). ★ The synth VEHICLE + import library are declared on the FORMAT descriptor (`librarySynthesis` in the .format.json), read by synth_threads_shim.cpp — pe→win32/kernel32.dll, macho→pthread/libSystem; the pass dispatches on that declared verb, never on a format identity (this dissolved the pass's former hardcoded kernel32.dll). Helper import names are applyCMangling-mangled per format (macho `_pthread_mutex_init`). ★ DUAL/TRIPLE SAME-NAME ENTRIES per function (the errno __error/__errno_location split precedent): a pe entry (["pe"] + `synthesize`), an elf entry (["elf"], plain FFI, no tag), and — for the 18 non-trampoline recipes — a macho entry (["macho"] + `synthesize`, its own pthread-width signature). The `synthesize` VALUE equals the function NAME (a validated invariant — the loader rejects a mismatch or an unknown recipe id, closed vocabulary). ★ __STDC_NO_THREADS__ is REMOVED from c.lang.json entirely: threads.h is COMPLETE on ALL legs (elf/pe64/macho — thrd_create/call_once/thrd_join landed on each), so a conforming impl must NOT define the macro anywhere (C11 6.10.8.3 / C23 6.10.9.3). ★ Cycle 2 LANDED thrd_create (pe DIRECT-PASS to CreateThread — the C11 int(*)(void*) start routine has the SAME x64 ABI as Win32 DWORD(*)(void*)), call_once (pe over InitOnceExecuteOnce via the module-scoped __dss_once_tramp adapter), thrd_join (pe multi-block: WaitForSingleObject; if(res) GetExitCodeThread; CloseHandle — StructCfMarkers rederived after finish()). ★ CYCLE 3 (P49 lane tw, D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TIMED) LANDED THE LAST FOUR: thrd_sleep, mtx_timedlock, cnd_timedwait and thrd_equal now carry a TRIPLE entry each (elf FFI + pe synth + macho synth) — see `$timedWaitsComment` below. ★ CYCLE 4 (P51 lane mx, D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-MACHO-MTX-PLAIN-RECURSIVE) CLOSED THE LAST ONE — `mtx_init`'s `type` argument is now HONOURED on macho, and nothing in this header is deferred any more. The macho recipe used to pass a NULL mutexattr; on Darwin a NULL attr is PTHREAD_MUTEX_DEFAULT == PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL, so `mtx_init(&m, mtx_plain | mtx_recursive)` returned a NON-recursive mutex and its owner's re-lock BLOCKED FOREVER — a hang, not a wrong value, and invisible to every compile-only pin. It now Allocas a 16-byte pthread_mutexattr_t, calls pthread_mutexattr_init/settype/destroy around pthread_mutex_init, and selects the kind BRANCHLESSLY from the type: `((type & mtx_recursive) != 0) * (PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE - PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL)`. It MASKS rather than compares, because C11 spells a recursive mutex as an OR — `mtx_timed | mtx_recursive` (3) is recursive too. ✔MEASURED on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL 0, ERRORCHECK 1, RECURSIVE **2** (NOT glibc's 1), DEFAULT 0, sizeof(pthread_mutexattr_t) 16, _Alignof 8 — and behaviourally, a NULL-attr relock did not return inside a 2 s bounded wait while a RECURSIVE-attr one returned at once. The row's stated obstacle — that an attr needs a stack Alloca and would break this pass's single-block/alloca-free invariant — was REFUTED: that invariant had already gone with Cycle 2's thrd_join and Cycle 3's timed recipes, and the fixed recipe is still ONE block. ★ THE pe HALF (D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-MTX-PLAIN-RECURSIVE) CLOSED WITHOUT A CODE CHANGE, on measurement rather than symmetry: a CRITICAL_SECTION is always recursion-capable, so pe already honours the only direction C11 constrains, and same-thread re-lock of an `mtx_plain` mutex is UNDEFINED (C11 7.26.4.3 / C23 7.28.4.3, a `shall` on the caller outside a Constraints clause). ✔MEASURED, the references disagree three ways on that exact program — glibc 2.39 BLOCKS (identically through gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3), MSVC 19.51's own <threads.h> FAIL-FAST ABORTS (0xC0000409), pe proceeds — so a recursion guard here would invent a fourth behaviour no reference requires. ⓘ Also measured and deliberately NOT copied: MSVC numbers the `thrd_*` status codes differently (thrd_error 4, thrd_timedout 2) while agreeing with glibc on all three `mtx_*` values above; C11 leaves the status values implementation-defined, and DSS's shims return values consistent with the `constants` block below. macho ONCE_FLAG_INIT diverges: macOS pthread_once_t needs the magic sig 0x30B1BCBA (816954554) in slot 0, so the ONCE_FLAG_INIT macro is a per-format variant ({0} elf/pe, {816954554} macho — the PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER-sig precedent). ★ TYPEDEF SIZES (per-format `variants`, mirroring pthread.json): thrd_t elf u64 (pthread_t) / pe ptr<void> (HANDLE) / macho u64. mtx_t elf arr<i64,6>=48 (pthread_mutex_t, arm64 MAX — over-allocates x86-64's 40 harmlessly) / pe arr<i64,5>=40 (CRITICAL_SECTION x64) / macho arr<i64,8>=64 (macOS pthread_mutex_t, measured). cnd_t elf/macho arr<i64,6>=48 (pthread_cond_t) / pe ptr<void>=8 (CONDITION_VARIABLE). once_flag elf i32 (pthread_once_t) / pe ptr<void>=8 (INIT_ONCE) / macho arr<i64,2>=16 (macOS pthread_once_t, measured). tss_t elf/pe u32 (glibc pthread_key_t + Win FLS DWORD) / macho u64 (macOS pthread_key_t=8 — DIVERGES; the macho tss_* signatures use u64). thrd_start_t = ptr<fn(ptr<void>)->i32> (the real C11 int(*)(void*) — Cycle 2, so `thrd_create(&t,worker,&arg)` accepts a bare `worker` cast-free). tss_dtor_t ptr<void>. thrd_t-by-VALUE fns (thrd_current/detach/join) diverge per format so their entries carry DIFFERENT signatures — the dual/triple-entry mechanism handles it. ★ CONSTANTS verified against glibc 2.39 threads.h: thrd_success=0/busy=1/error=2/nomem=3/timedout=4; mtx_plain=0/recursive=1/timed=2 — the SAME values the pe + macho recipes return, so a witness comparing ==thrd_success is portable.
$timedWaitsComment: D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TIMED (P49 lane tw, 2026-09-01) — the FOUR C11 <threads.h> functions that were undeclared on EVERY format while `__STDC_NO_THREADS__` is defined on none: `thrd_sleep` (elf-only until now), `mtx_timedlock`, `cnd_timedwait`, `thrd_equal`. ★ THE ELF ARMS ARE PLAIN FFI AND EVERY SYMBOL WAS ✔MEASURED PRESENT BEFORE BEING DECLARED (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT: one absent name breaks the LOAD of every binary built against this descriptor, not just the callers). `nm -D --defined-only libc.so.6`, glibc 2.39, on BOTH elf legs — x86_64 (WSL) and aarch64 (the native arm64 VPS): `thrd_equal@@GLIBC_2.28` T, `thrd_sleep@@GLIBC_2.28` **W** (a WEAK definition, which the eager-import law permits — an ABSENT one does not), `mtx_timedlock@@GLIBC_2.34` T, `cnd_timedwait@@GLIBC_2.34` T. ⚠ `readelf --dyn-syms` TRUNCATES long names to `cnd_[...]@@GLIBC_2.34` and answered `mtx_timedlock` NOT FOUND on a libc that exports it; `nm -D` is the instrument that does not lie here. ★ THE pe AND macho ARMS ARE `synthesize` RECIPES over the same per-vehicle mechanism the other 21 use (win32/kernel32 · pthread/libSystem), because neither platform exports the C11 names: ucrtbase/kernel32 export no `thrd_*`, and Darwin's libSystem exports none either (✔MEASURED by LINK PROBE — `nm`/`dyld_info` CANNOT answer this on macOS 26, where /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib is not a file on disk but a dyld-shared-cache entry, and both instruments report ZERO for every symbol including `_nanosleep`, which certainly exists; the linker is the oracle). ★★ THE pe RECIPES READ `struct timespec` AT THE LAYOUT time.json's OWN pe ARM DECLARES — tv_sec `long long` 8B @0, tv_nsec **`long` 4B** @8 — which is the prerequisite this row was gated on and which P49 lane th measured with a `_Static_assert` battery on mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51.36252 separately, each with a deliberately-false control arm. A shim that read tv_nsec as 8 bytes would fold the struct's trailing pad into the nanoseconds field; `examples/c/c11_threads_timed` POISONS the struct to 0xFF before assigning, so that exact miscompile is a RUNTIME red rather than an invisible one. ★ macho reads tv_nsec as 8 bytes (Darwin is LP64 — ✔MEASURED by a RUN probe on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: sizeof 16, tv_sec@0/8, tv_nsec@8/8, _Alignof 8, sizeof(long)=8), matching this file's macho `timespec` arm. ★ SIGNATURE DIVERGENCE: `thrd_equal` takes thrd_t BY VALUE, and thrd_t is `ptr<void>` (a HANDLE) on pe against `u64` on elf/macho — so the pe entry carries `fn(ptr<void>, ptr<void>) -> i32` and the other two `fn(u64, u64) -> i32`, exactly as thrd_current/thrd_detach/thrd_join already do. ⚠ `mtx_timedlock` HAS NO NATIVE PRIMITIVE ON EITHER SYNTH PLATFORM and that is measured, not assumed: `TryEnterCriticalSection` carries no timeout, and `pthread_mutex_timedlock` is ABSENT FROM DARWIN (link probe: every other primitive in the same battery — pthread_cond_timedwait, nanosleep, pthread_equal, clock_gettime, gettimeofday, mach_absolute_time — LINKS; that one does not). Both arms are therefore trylock/deadline LOOPS, and the loop is the implementation rather than a workaround: the platform offers no other construction. `cnd_timedwait` DOES have one on both (SleepConditionVariableCS · pthread_cond_timedwait) and is a single block on each.
